newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch industry aims for 15-20pct of euro airfreight.
newsitem.headline: Dutch industry aims for 15-20pct of euro airfreight.

text.p: The Dutch airfreight industry is aiming for a 15 to 20 percent share of the European air cargo market by the year 2020, representing 7.5 to 10 million tonnes of cargo a year.

The ambition to become a leading European player in the airfreight industry was announced in a report "Space for Freight" produced by ATAN, the Air Transport Association in the Netherlands, Amsterdam Airport Schiphol and KLM Cargo in cooperation with KPMG Peat Marwick LLP.

In the report the industry states that six to seven million tonnes of this cargo would be handled by the Dutch mainport and the rest of the cargo would be accommodated by foreign airport infrastructure, not regional Dutch airports.

The Dutch airfreight industry wants to improve its standard airfreight services and the high valued services such as integrated logistics, as well as express transport through the development of better same-day delivery services.
These developments would give the Dutch economy an enormous boost, the report stated. At the moment, the airfreight industry is worth 9.3 billion guilders ($4.8 billion) to the Dutch economy.

In 1995, 75,000 people were employed, directly or indirectly, by the industry. KPMG stated that the new strategy, if successful, will mean an increase in job numbers by 4.5 percent a year, rising to 225,000 in the year 2020.
However, for the plan to be successful, the industry needs integrated products with adequate information technology.

Enough airfreight capacity in one central location is also crucial but the mainport must have enough infrastructure to facilitate efficient transport lines, whether they are by road, rail or underground systems.
The next phase following the report is to develop a joint policy to put the plan into action.

Invesigations are going to be carried out into how the Netherlands night-time capacity can be used more efficiently. Environmental transport and underground transport options will also be investigated. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017 - www.racs.com ($ = 1.939 Dutch Guilders)
